title: Coral and the Asset
premise: Silas Galloway, a disgraced financial-crimes investigator hiding in a dead-end compliance job, receives a meeting invitation from his former handler—sent three days after her funeral. The invitation leads him to Coral Vance, the handler's estranged daughter, who has inherited not just her mother's apartment but an encrypted ledger proving that a sanctioned slush fund Silas once helped bury is still moving money through three governments. Hunted by an assassin called the Cartographer and betrayed by the agency that trained him, Silas and Coral race across Lisbon, Vienna, and Trieste to deliver the ledger before a dawn extraction flight. In the end, Silas chooses exposure over escape, testifying remotely as the flight takes off without him—and survives because the truth, once loose, makes him too dangerous to kill.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money she was never allowed to name. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Insomniac and gray, Silas audits clean money by day and rereads old case files by night. An email arrives from his dead handler, Nadia Vance, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at a Lisbon café he hasn't visited in six years. The beat: dread sharpening into compulsion—he goes.

chapters.title: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the café, no one comes—until a young woman sits down uninvited: Coral Vance, Nadia's daughter, holding her mother's phone. She received the same invitation. Someone wanted them both here. The beat: wary alliance between two strangers bound by grief.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sorting Nadia's apartment, Coral finds a hidden safe behind her mother's sewing machine: a burner phone, a key, and one line of instructions naming Silas. The beat: resentment curdling into curiosity—who was her mother, really?

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The key opens a deposit box containing a hardware wallet: the Meridian ledger, tracking a sanctioned slush fund Silas helped bury years ago—still active, still laundering through three governments' quiet accounts. The beat: the past isn't past; it's compounding interest.

chapters.title: Cartography of Death
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed). A meticulous killer known as the Cartographer maps Silas's routines like terrain, noting he never sleeps before 4 a.m. Orders arrive: retrieve the ledger, leave no witnesses. The beat: cold professional patience—the reader sees the trap closing.

chapters.title: Runners
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas spots surveillance outside Coral's building and pulls her out through the tram tunnels he memorized during his informant years. First contact with the enemy; they barely escape. The beat: fear becoming momentum—they're in it now.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decoding messages on the burner phone, Coral learns her mother spent years secretly rebuilding the case Silas abandoned—and died the week she finished. The beat: grief reframed as inheritance; anger at Silas for walking away.

chapters.title: Old Contacts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas reaches out to Tomas, a retired colleague in Vienna, seeking a way to authenticate the ledger. Tomas agrees—but Silas notices the man's fear, and realizes word of the ledger has already spread. The beat: trust as a dwindling resource.

chapters.title: Night Train
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lisbon to Vienna overnight. On the train, Coral and Silas trade their histories—her rootless childhood, his self-imposed exile—and begin to trust. But a passenger photographs them. The beat: intimacy blooming under threat.

chapters.title: Vienna Station
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Cartographer intercepts Tomas first, extracting the meeting location. When Silas and Coral arrive, the safehouse is already turned over; Tomas is gone. The beat: every step forward costs someone else.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Reading the ledger fully, Silas maps its beneficiaries: officials in Portugal, Austria, and Italy, all fed through a shell network he once helped design. His own fingerprints are on the architecture. The beat: complicity—he can't just expose it; he must confess it.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A final scheduled message from Nadia plays on the burner: instructions for a journalist contact in Trieste and a warning—'the agency will offer you safety. It will be the trap.' The beat: posthumous guidance, a mother's voice reaching across death.

chapters.title: Offer of Sanctuary
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas's old deputy director calls: come in, full protection, witness program. Exactly what Nadia predicted. Silas stalls, then discovers the 'safe house' address matches a property in the ledger. The beat: disillusionment—the institution itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Driving to Trieste, they're boxed in on a mountain road. A chase ends with Coral driving off-road while Silas destroys the decoy drive they've carried since Lisbon. The Cartographer retrieves the fake—and knows he's been played. The beat: cunning as survival.

chapters.title: Trieste
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hiding in a fisherman's attic above the Adriatic, Coral decrypts the final layer of the ledger using her mother's birthday—a detail only family would know. The beat: belonging found in inheritance; the vault was always meant for her.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Meeting Nadia's journalist contact, Elena Marchetti, Silas offers everything—including his own role—in exchange for publication before dawn. Elena warns: once it runs, there's no country left that will hide him. The beat: the cost made explicit.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Molo
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Cartographer, having traced the decoy's failure, corners them at the harbor warehouse where the exchange is set. Tomas, alive and coerced, reveals their location. The beat: the net closes; sacrifice becomes unavoidable.

chapters.title: Warehouse Fire
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A firefight in the burning warehouse; Tomas redeems himself by tackling the Cartographer long enough for Silas and Coral to escape with the ledger, but doesn't survive. The beat: loss transmuted into obligation—finish it for the dead.

chapters.title: Extraction at Dawn
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the airfield, the agency's extraction plane waits—one seat, one passenger, deniability guaranteed. Elena's story publishes online as engines start. Silas puts Coral aboard with the authenticated copy and stays behind. The beat: choosing truth over escape.

chapters.title: Too Public to Kill
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Cartographer has Silas in his sights on the tarmac when the story detonates globally—three governments scrambling, the fund frozen, Silas's confession trending worldwide. Killing him now creates a martyr and confirms the ledger. He lowers the gun. The beat: survival through exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later, Coral watches Silas testify via video link from protective custody, naming names including his own. Resignations cascade. She visits her mother's grave and finally understands what Nadia built and why. The beat: justice as slow, imperfect inheritance.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Months later, Silas—cleared but changed—meets Coral in Lisbon at the same café. For the first time since the incident, he slept through the night. They order two coffees and plan what comes next. The beat: belonging earned; memory honored; rest at last.
